title: The walls of Jericho (Joshua 6)
hookLine: six days of silent circling, then shofar blasts and a shout
last: STAND STILL, AND KNOW WHERE YOU ARE.

cards: For six days, the only sound around Jericho is the shofar. Armed men walk in front. Then seven priests, blowing seven rams' horns as they go.
Then the ark. Then everyone else. Row after row of feet, and not one human voice.
The instruction was clear: no shouting, no talking, not a word from your mouth until the day you're told. Once around the walls, back to the camp for the night. The next morning, again.
Behind its walls, Jericho is shut tight, facing an army that doesn't attack.

teach.h: SEVEN TIMES ON THE SEVENTH DAY.
teach.b: On the seventh day they rise at dawn and go around, not once, but seven times. On the seventh circuit the priests blow, and Joshua finally gives the word: shout, for the Lord has given you the city.
The people raise a great shout, and "the wall fell down flat." Notice what the story leaves out: no battering ram, no ladders, no tunnel under the wall.
The city falls to a strange discipline: patience, silence, repetition, and then one sound at the right moment.

teach.h: TERUAH: A SHOUT, A SHOFAR CALL.
teach.b: The instruction had said it plainly: no word from your mouth until the day I bid you shout, "then shall ye shout." The Hebrew for that great shout is teruah. It's also the name of a shofar call.
The Torah calls Rosh Hashanah a day of teruah, a day of blowing the horn. So one word holds a people's cry and the ram's horn of the new year.
Some readers hear in Jericho a picture of the Days of Awe: circle, wait, keep quiet, and then let out the sound you've been holding. And there's a hard part, and the book doesn't hide it.
The city is put under the ban, and its people are killed, and readers wrestle with that command. Inside the destruction, one promise holds.
Before the city burns, the two spies go into Rahab's house and bring out her and her whole family, as they swore they would. The spies kept their word.

how: On Rosh Hashanah the shofar is sounded in synagogue in a set series of calls, among them teruah, a run of quick short blasts.

games.q: it's the fourth day of walking around Jericho in silence. nothing has happened. you're walking behind the ark. what do you do?
o: shout anyway, to rattle the city.
keep walking in silence, as told.
drop out and wait in the camp.
games.why: the order was no word until the day Joshua says shout. the silence lasted six days, then seven more circuits.

practice: Walk slowly around something in silence, a table, a bed, the room you're in, once and then again, noticing your feet and the edges you usually pass without seeing.
If you can't walk, let your eyes travel slowly around the edges of the room instead. When you stop, let the quiet settle before anything else is said.
